subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a public browser navigation deny/warn policy, and what traffic classes must it cover across top-level navigation, redirects, subframes, subresources, downloads, and browser proxy profiles?
rationale: This would create an operator-trusted browser security/config boundary, so automation should not choose permanent denylist, warnlist, default-list, or path-matching semantics without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-scoped block and warning semantics before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Egress Policy
options.body: Let the generic egress-firewall direction own browser navigation too, but only after it explicitly covers browser-specific behavior.

options.title: Advisory Hints Only
options.body: Avoid an enforceable denylist and only surface best-effort warnings for known bot-blocked sites.

recommendation.title: Design Browser Policy Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser-scoped block and warning semantics before implementation.
